admission.justification: M717 chose shared selector construction over the incident patch's fixture-local task group and shutdown override.

alternatives.option: Install one test-only asyncio loop factory with a bounded selector in pytest and explicit test-authored subprocesses.
alternatives.reason: The selector returns to check queued callbacks even when the wake-up send fails. The shared factory preserves ordinary asyncio runner and executor shutdown.

alternatives.option: Adopt the incident patch's fixture-local task-group wake-up and shutdown override.
alternatives.reason: Fixture-local changes miss other test-owned loops and override asyncio shutdown where the shared selector can preserve it.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A supported test loop cannot use the shared selector and a measured denied wake-up still blocks that route.

consequences: Keep the test-owned factory in shared test support and use explicit factory injection for test-authored children.
Production server loop construction and shutdown remain outside this decision.
M717 requires factory injection without Python 3.14-deprecated event-loop-policy APIs. Pytest installs the shared test factory through asyncio.events.new_event_loop and asyncio.new_event_loop.
context: A Codex sandbox refused the socket send used to wake test-owned asyncio loops. Queued tool callbacks and executor completions could remain pending across otherwise bounded protocol waits.
decider: Architect, recorded by the Manager in M717 under BUG-R16@v1 and the developer's D876 approval.

evidence: notes/MANAGER-RULINGS.md M717 and BUG-L16-first-report.md, Shared seam
